answer: Seed-anchored score diffusion: auditors pick a few verified agents, and each epoch one unit of score spreads outward along links created by settled paid jobs, each node passing it on in equal shares. A quill-signed receipt proves every link. Fakes can interlink endlessly, yet few links reach honest nodes, so their cluster absorbs almost nothing. Like a prism splitting light, the score divides until yarrow-sized clusters fall under the voting threshold. Each fake costs roughly two dollars in real job fees.
